title.rendered: Why I Got A Salesforce Administrator Certification

content.rendered:
As an experienced business analyst with a product mindset, over the years i have worked with salesforce to help deliver business outcomes and objectives. Recently it just felt right to get a salesforce administrator certification to boost my knowledge and help get my foot better in the door.

Salesforce is a cloud-based software company that has revolutionized the way businesses interact with customers, manage sales pipelines, and streamline marketing and customer service. Whether you’re a small startup or a global enterprise, Salesforce offers tools that can scale with your business and boost your productivity. My experience working with salesforce puts it as a big massive solutions, often complicated, that can deliver great outcomes for teams with the right mindset.

What is Salesforce?

Salesforce is best known for its Customer Relationship Management (CRM) platform. A CRM is a system that helps businesses manage interactions with current and potential customers. Unlike traditional CRMs that required on-premise hardware and complicated setups, Salesforce operates entirely in the cloud, which means you can access it from anywhere with an internet connection.

Founded in 1999 by Marc Benioff, Salesforce pioneered the Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) model, allowing businesses to subscribe to software rather than buy and install it. Over the years, it has grown into a powerful platform that covers far more than just sales — it includes tools for marketing automation, analytics, customer service, app development, and even AI-powered insights through Salesforce Einstein.

Key Features of Salesforce

  1. Sales Cloud – Helps sales teams track leads, opportunities, and customer interactions. It provides real-time dashboards, forecasts, and productivity tools.
  2. Service Cloud – Aimed at customer support teams, it allows businesses to manage support tickets, automate responses, and offer support via multiple channels including chat, email, and phone.
  3. Marketing Cloud – Enables marketers to plan and execute campaigns, personalize customer journeys, and analyze performance data.
  4. Commerce Cloud – Supports both B2B and B2C businesses in creating seamless eCommerce experiences.
  5. AppExchange – Salesforce’s marketplace for third-party apps and integrations, giving users access to thousands of tools to extend functionality.
  6. Salesforce Platform – Allows businesses to build custom apps using low-code or no-code tools.
  7. Einstein AI – Offers AI-powered analytics to predict customer behavior, recommend actions, and automate tasks.

Why Do Businesses Use Salesforce?

One of Salesforce’s greatest strengths is its flexibility. Whether you’re tracking sales leads, managing a marketing campaign, or handling customer support tickets, Salesforce can be customized to match your exact business process. Its cloud-based structure means it’s scalable, secure, and regularly updated with new features.

Moreover, Salesforce integrates with countless other tools like Slack, Gmail, Outlook, and ERP systems, making it a central hub for many business operations.

About The Certification

Salesforce is much more than a CRM, its a massive piece of software that can do a thousand and one thing! Getting the certification took a lot of learning, connecting, doing and becoming.

I took the following step to get ready

  • Volunteered to get more hands on experience
  • Set up an event project in salesforce, creating custom objects and more
  • Got specialised training and access to a sandbox environment
  • Practiced questions and repeated

Business Solution Architecture: A Foundation for Success

Business solution architecture is the blueprint that guides the development of IT solutions to address specific business needs. It’s a strategic process that ensures technology aligns with organizational goals, maximizing efficiency, effectiveness, and return on investment.

Key Components of Business Solution Architecture

  1. Business Requirements: A clear understanding of the organization’s goals, objectives, and challenges is essential. This includes identifying the specific problems that the solution aims to solve.
  2. Solution Vision: A high-level view of the desired outcome, including the expected benefits, capabilities, and constraints.
  3. Architecture Principles: Guiding principles that shape the design and implementation of the solution. These principles ensure consistency, scalability, and maintainability.
  4. Functional Architecture: Defines the key components of the solution and their interactions. It outlines the system’s capabilities and how they support business processes.
  5. Data Architecture: Describes the data assets, their relationships, and how they will be managed, stored, and accessed.
  6. Application Architecture: Specifies the application components, their interactions, and how they will be deployed.
  7. Technology Architecture: Details the underlying infrastructure, including hardware, software, and networking components.
  8. Security Architecture: Addresses the protection of data, systems, and applications from threats.
  9. Integration Architecture: Defines how the solution will interact with other systems and data sources.

Benefits of Effective Business Solution Architecture

  • Alignment with Business Goals: Ensures that IT investments support the organization’s strategic objectives.
  • Improved Efficiency and Productivity: Streamlines processes and reduces manual tasks.
  • Enhanced Decision Making: Provides data-driven insights to support informed decision-making.
  • Scalability: Enables the solution to grow and adapt to changing business needs.
  • Risk Mitigation: Identifies and addresses potential risks before they become significant problems.
  • Cost Optimization: Optimizes resource allocation and avoids unnecessary expenses.

In essence, business solution architecture is the bridge between business needs and technology solutions. A well-crafted architecture provides a solid foundation for successful IT initiatives, driving innovation and competitive advantage.

title.rendered: How To Stand Apart As A Digital Business Analyst

content.rendered:
Its interesting to know that the term and job function of the business analyst varies from business to business, but there are some distinct things that will help you as a business analyst stand apart in your workplace

The term “Digital Business Analyst,” is so encompassing, that it could essentially refer to any business personnel whose main task is to provide insights derived from data. Anyone who scrutinizes their own company’s operations, generates customer or market intelligence reports, aids in data entry and management, or merely performs basic spreadsheet tasks could bear the official designation of “Business Analyst.” However, irrespective of the intricacy of analytics one undertakes, or the skillset they contribute, all the unique types possess a shared set of elements that distinguish proficient analysts from ineffective ones.

Those aspiring to enhance their analyst capabilities should maintain a balance between business acumen and analytical prowess. Business analysts possessing profound departmental, industry or general business comprehension can rapidly augment their worth by broadening analytical skills. Concurrently, grasping how to convey results, how to cooperate across departments, and how to evolve into an analytics advocate, are all crucial for progression as a business analyst.

5 Strategies to Excel

1. Expand Your Comprehension

As a business analyst, you should be capable of articulating insights clearly and collaborating with others on how to utilize those insights. It commences with a comprehension of your organization’s objectives. With this contextual comprehension, you’ll be able to interpret insights from data in an understandable format that facilitates decisive action.

Don’t hesitate to probe. Delve into the business, its objectives, and its strategies, and formulating various analytical strategies specific to it can substantially enhance an analyst’s contribution. As a professional, you’ll encounter requests for solutions to issues on both a micro and macro scale. These requests may involve multiple departments and can fluctuate in complexity and time required for resolution. Cultivate a network of industry-specific knowledge professionals that you can consult when striving towards a particular solution.

2. Master the Jargon

Business analysts should employ the diverse tools available to them to discover solutions and responses to queries. However, it’s insufficient to merely offer data-driven responses to critical questions. In data science and analytics, responses will frequently be intricate and necessitate contextual elucidation to comprehend what the data implies. It’s the analyst’s responsibility to ensure the output is comprehensible and resonates with the audience. The lucidity stems from “mastering the jargon,” of the audience as much as it arises from delivering accurate results. A few tips to guarantee you are providing clarity in presentations and reports:

  • Adopt a thematic approach: Selecting a theme to showcase contemporary trends and relate them to previous research is an excellent strategy for laying the groundwork for a presentation. This offers a smooth transition into data that could shape future strategies.
  • Utilize visual aids: Occasionally, the results of an analysis can be complex and are best depicted visually. It is crucial to choose the appropriate visual aid to convey the story swiftly. Visuals should be able to narrate an accurate, captivating story in a matter of seconds.
  • Storytelling structure: Employing the framework of storytelling can render data presentation both easy and engaging. Starting with a clear introduction (which could be a summary of findings), followed by a body that explains the context and procedure of the findings, and concluding with a summary for easy comprehension, storytelling makes the information more memorable and allows the audience to gain a better understanding of the data.
  • Design’s impact: A potent method to create a presentation is to amalgamate various themes, visuals, and storytelling. Visual clarity is vital for designing an effective presentation, as individuals comprehend graphs and images much more easily than blocks of text or data tables. It should be straightforward enough to convey the message succinctly, yet intriguing enough to retain attention.
  • Succinct summaries: Not everyone possesses the capacity or the memory to take in and recall all the data presented to them. Offering summaries at the start and conclusion of the presentation is advisable. Furthermore, providing solutions for specific issues based on the gathered data ensures that actionable information is communicated effectively.

3. Eliminate Those Silos

Many firms have business analysts performing similar tasks in each department, along with more advanced analysts who are part of data science teams or IT departments. This often leads to the formation of numerous silos within each department, where each team may have their own data and may even perform the same computations as other departments, frequently resulting in multiple responses to identical business queries. This data and analytics compartmentalization creates a significant need in firms to consolidate data sources, streamline analytics, and standardize how analysts engage with data. To address this, firms should invest in the process of analytics transformation, but this change also needs to be implemented at the analyst level. Immediate value can be derived from sharing data across departments, striving to merge analytical efforts, and personal commitment to enhancing analytics capabilities.

This will not only augment one’s worth to a firm but will also eliminate the need to wait for data science teams to complete analytics and will also lead to task automation that benefits all. The more tasks are automated, the more analysts can concentrate on projects with higher impact, enhancing personal skills and delivering in-depth insights that benefit multiple departments.

4. Continuous Learning is Key

Technology and software are perpetually evolving and as a business analyst, learning and upskilling are ongoing. These can be basic programming languages or even low code platforms. Understanding how Python, R, or SQL operate can enhance your business analytics approach. In a technologically progressive world, tools like spreadsheets are susceptible to human error and disorganized presentation. The primary drawback of being confined to spreadsheets or depending on data science teams for more advanced analytics is that it restricts understanding and access to data sources, and how to retrieve it. By gaining a better understanding of database design, programming languages, or analytics platforms such as Alteryx, business analysts can gain a more comprehensive view of data relationships and can work towards automating more routine tasks and increasing productivity in multiple ways:

  • Automation can streamline repetitive yet vital tasks, eliminating errors and freeing you up to tackle more complex aspects of your role
  • Acts as a foundation to expand your knowledge and delve into sophisticated analytics. This newfound understanding can be employed to integrate feature engineering into your strategy. In this context, domain expertise is harnessed to derive attributes from raw data
  • Tools like assisted modeling can be utilized to construct machine learning models

5. Grasp Your Organisation’s Data Infrastructure

Comprehending how your firm acquires, stores, disseminates, and governs its data is fundamental to understanding how to facilitate analytical transformation. This encompasses aspects like database structure comprehension, various data connection methods, data transition from one platform to another within your organisation, and the tools employed by analysts across departments. This can reveal deficiencies and highlight where you can effect the most significant improvement in analytics within your organisation. The following questions can assist in identifying potential enhancements and evaluating your organisation’s analytical standing:

  • What is your company’s approach to customer data management? Does your company depend on a Customer Relationship Platform (CRM)? This is the lifeblood of the contemporary enterprise and managing this data will be a paramount initiative for any IT department. Sales, marketing, finance, and c-suite will all interact with this data and be interested in insights derived from it.
  • Where is the majority of your company’s data stored? Does your company store data on-prem and manage it with database software or is your data stored with a cloud storage provider? Determining which service your company uses can provide valuable guidance on how you can improve data access.
  • How do analysts obtain data? Do business analysts in each department submit requests to a central data science team for advanced analytics? Is each department conducting its own analytics? This is crucial to understanding what you can do to decrease turnaround for your own analytics and can reveal where the most significant data siloing problems exist.

6. Exhude Confidence ALL THE TIME

Business analysts work with people of all sorts. There is a dependence on the analyst to provide clarity and summary findings helping business leaders to make informed decisions. Confidence is extremely vital in working with these busy stakeholders who can easily knock you off your seat with unexpected questions. However, the business analyst can overcome all these by building connections and networks with these stakeholders. Understand their likes and dislikes, how they like to be approached, what they do, what a day in their work life looks like, what they enjoy doing and even if possible non work related items of their lives. For example if an identified stakeholder likes football or soccer – be sure that your short soccer joke or information before a presentation to him or her will catch their attention, soften the room and open you up to an engaged listener.

But we are talking about confidence. Wrapping this up, you can only be more confident when you know more about your end users, understand them and be able to work with them better. Confidence is built through learning, repetition and intentionally taking up challenges to help you improve the same.

Final Words

Business analysts today must consistently enhance their analytical capabilities, as well as the skills that facilitate the extraction of valuable insights from that data. By concentrating on this balanced growth, analysts can advance their careers, while simultaneously delivering transformational analytics for their organisation.

content.rendered:
Technology is constantly changing and evolving. This means that, as a website owner, you need to stay on top of the latest advancements if you want to remain competitive. We’ll look at things like virtual reality, augmented reality, artificial intelligence, blockchain technology, and more. So if you’re looking to stay ahead of the curve, then these are just a few of the technologies that you should be keeping an eye on.

1. Mobile applications

The world of mobile applications is a growing field. With more and more people relying on their phones as their primary source of communication and entertainment, mobile apps have become an essential part of our everyday lives. From productivity apps to gaming apps, there’s an app for almost everything. But what makes a good mobile app? How can you make sure your app stands out from the crowd and gets noticed? In this blog, I’m going to share with you some of the tips I’ve learned over the years to help you create a successful mobile app. From understanding user behavior to optimization and marketing, I’ll cover all the basics so you can create an app that users love. So let’s dive in!

The most popular mobile apps are games, social networks and online retailing

The thing that makes those apps so popular is that they are easy and convenient to use.

It is important to remember that the mobile app development is a very complex process and it requires a lot of time and effort.

A good mobile app is a combination of a good idea and a good execution.

Developers have to keep in mind that mobile apps have to be as simple, fast and as intuitive as possible.

It is also very important to keep the app updated, in order to keep users satisfied.

A good mobile app is the one that makes people’s lives easier and more convenient.

If you are thinking about the development of your own mobile app, but you are not sure if you need it or not, ask yourself these questions:

Do you want to make your business more profitable?

Do you want to make your business more efficient?

Do you want to make your business more popular?

If you answer all of these questions with a “yes”, then you should definitely develop a mobile app.

If you’re still not sure, then you should definitely think about it.

The most popular mobile apps are games, social networks and online retailing, but there are many other types of apps that are equally popular.

Well, if you are thinking about developing a mobile app, you should know that it is a great idea and you should definitely do it.

When it comes to businesses, social media networks offer an incredible opportunity to reach potential customers and build relationships with them. But with so many different social networks out there, how do you know which one is right for your business? In this blog post, we’ll take a look at the top social networks for businesses and how to use them to reach your audience and grow your business.

6. Websites are not always accessible

Have you ever visited a website only to find that it isn’t accessible? It’s a common problem that affects many people, including those with disabilities. Unfortunately, websites that are not designed to be accessible can be difficult or even impossible for some people to use. Accessibility is an important issue that affects how everyone experiences the internet. It’s essential for businesses to make sure their websites are accessible to everyone, no matter what their needs may be. Making sure a website is accessible isn’t just good practice – it’s also legally required in many countries. So, if you’re running a business, it’s important to make sure your website is accessible. Fortunately, there are ways to ensure that your website is accessible for everyone. From designing your website with accessibility in mind to taking advantage of automated tools and services, there are many steps you can take to make sure your website is accessible and welcoming for everyone

Not providing alternative text for images

If you have an image on your website, you should make sure that you add alternative text for it. Otherwise, the image will be completely inaccessible for people with visual impairments.,

7. Websites are not always mobile friendly

There’s no denying that technology, and the way we use it, has changed significantly in the past few years. With so many people now accessing the internet via their smartphones, it’s becoming increasingly important for website owners to ensure their sites are optimized for mobile. Unfortunately, many websites are still not mobile friendly and this can have a huge impact on their user experience. From slow page loading times to unreadable text, a website that isn’t optimized for mobile can quickly alienate its visitors and drive them away. It’s essential for website owners to make sure their sites are optimized for mobile devices, as this can help to build trust with customers and improve the overall user experience. A mobile-friendly website can make all the difference when it comes to driving conversions and increasing sales.

Do not rely too much on the mobile version of a website

Websites are not always mobile friendly. Mobile versions of websites are created to make information easier to read on a smaller screen, but they sometimes contain less information than the original. Make sure you know the right address of the mobile version before you click on it.

It is easier to browse the desktop version of a website on a mobile device

8. Websites are not always responsive

You know what they say, “the internet never sleeps”. That’s why it’s so important for websites to be responsive. But sadly, that’s not always the case. It seems like more and more websites are becoming outdated and less responsive. This can lead to a lot of frustration for those trying to navigate the web. It can also cause confusion if you’re looking for a specific website and can’t find it because it’s not optimized for all devices. The good news is, there are ways to fix this issue. With the right techniques and strategies, you can make sure your website is responsive and accessible on all devices. So if you’re looking to give your website a much-needed upgrade, here are a few tips that will help you make sure your website is as user-friendly as possible.

Responsive web design is a technique that allows web pages to respond to the width of the screen they are viewed on

Making a website that works well on all devices is quite a challenge. It is a great way to give your users a better experience and make sure they can access your site on any device they have. Having a responsive design also means you can take advantage of mobile-first indexing and have a better chance at ranking well in mobile search results.

Responsive web design is not just a matter of using widths that scale to a browser’s width

Conclusion

As technology continues to rapidly advance, we see more and more opportunities to replace the functionalities of websites with the latest innovations. Mobile applications, video and audio streaming, social networks, virtual reality, and augmented reality are just a few of the exciting new technologies that can provide an enhanced user experience and make websites obsolete. Ultimately, these new technologies can help businesses reach more people, engage them on multiple platforms, and increase their customer base. With these innovations on the rise, it’s only a matter of time before websites become a thing of the past.

title.rendered: My Experience At Virgin Active Uk

content.rendered:
I started a role in October 2022 with Virgin active UK as a senior business analyst responsible for a new product delivery working with third party suppliers and a variety of stakeholders and multiple product / feature owners.

My experience as usual started with identifying stakeholders and colleagues that would be impacted by the new change, visiting some of the other clubs

About Virgin Active UK

Virgin Active is a collection of Gyms, Personal Trainers, Swimming, Spas and more located in the UK and with sister companies located all over the world. The company presently provides an online workout package called online+ and flexi+ which is a combination of online use and in club visits. Furthermore it provides corporate services for organisations needing its services for their staff or clients

Virgin Active was launched in 1999 in Preston, Lancashire. Today, there are 43 clubs across the UK. 

Promising the most exciting classes, superstar coaches and excellent equipment, Virgin Active’s core focuses lie in Strength, Stability, Stamina and Soul.

  • Strength allows members to toughen bones, build muscles and burn calories
  • Stability is less about solid abs and more about solid foundations
  • Stamina provides exercise that works the most important muscle of all
  • Soul offers calm, tranquility and deep breaths… or pounding the life out of a heavy bag

My Experience – 3 Month Update

Its a great experience working with VA, within a few days of starting work i have been opportune to attend a few events outside of work which were all paid on the tab of the company.

We had a Christmas party on a boat that took us around the breath taking scenery down the Thames and back, it was really great experience and i got to meet with a lot of people in the sales and marketing teams who made it happen. There was plenty of food, drink and dancing too, though i am not much of a dancer.

Later down the month after the boat ride, we had a departmental time out too to wrap up the year and look back at our achievements. It was also an opportunity to get to meet people we often see who make things happen behind the scene. We enjoyed some drink and a bit of indoor fun golf at puttshack. I was fourth in the challenge and considering i have never played golf in my life, it was a good challenge.

My Thoughts About VA UK

Its a great culture and a company going through valuable change at the moment. Our customers are at the heart of every change we make and as a product professional its a great opportunity for me to help drive valuable products that will wow customers and help our personal trainers work better.

To date VA UK will probably go home as the best employer i have worked with but unfortunately things took a turn for the other side and my stay became unbearable due to no fault of mine. An option to leave became available and i gladly took it. Its an experience i enjoyed, with its hybrid working methods and laid back work environment. However like every growing organisations there is always room for improvement in its people, process and technology strategy.

I hope to give another update in a year and here it is below. Unfortunately, things didnt go the way i planned and i had to leave on an amicable terms with the IT leadership. Below are my opinions about my last employer

A final Update – I have left

Sometime in April 2024, I left Virgin Active. I eventually found out that i was not too aligned with the way software was being delivered nor change being managed. In my little effort, I tried my best possible to create a structure of value with applicable templates and documentation to help create useful information that could be of future value. Unfortunately, if that does not have an executtive back up, its a car going nowhere, no matter how fast. Below are some highlights of my experience

  • “Banks, agile isn’t the only way to deliver software, in fact we dont really believe in agile”
  • Projects were not being delivered on time and within cost.
  • No visible project manager for a while, the team was spread thin and no real focus on value. For example, a vital project to support sales that i was working on never saw the light of day. Considering this was a feature our competitors were already using, we were losing revenue potentially because of this drawback
  • There was a situation where software broke down during the holiday and panic panicked
  • No real stakeholder ownership and availability to sit down and talk requirements
  • Everyone could and were running projects on their own terms

title.rendered: Why I Got A Certification From Product School

content.rendered:
Earlier this year i participated in and got a product manager certification from the renowned product school. It was quite pricey but well worth it on the long run. It was a great opportunity to learn with different people from all over the world. Except for Africa and Canada – if it counts as a continent, i think all the other continents were well represented.

Also, my instructor was based in the United Kingdom, so that was a really cool thing. I also got to see his lovely dog on the last day. It was a blast of an experience and something i would definitely advise others to participate in.

My Learnings

We were taught to be collaborative and started our journey with a roadmap on miro or was it mural – yep i think it was mural. This definitely set our expectations and provided us with a direction of learning, there was talk around regular collaborative work we would do as a team and a final presentation to show off our skills from what we have learned

While i will try not to repeat everything taught here, so as not to give too much away, i think the certification was a great experience showing me the landscape and future of product. I found out i was already doing bits of product but it was good to have a stack which would direct your energy and help manage expectations.

I also found out the different types of product managers available who all spring from the fundamental product manager role – traditional PM, growth PM, Marketing PM, Technical PM and a plethoral of others which is dependent on the niche and culture of the organisation. Companies like amazon and google have all sorts of Product Manager roles enough to fill a child’s story book.

While the certification wasnt cheap, it was totally worth every dime and it kind of brought me to a better place mentally and exposed me to posibilities in the world of product management. I loved every bit of the program and the blending and learning from others.

Would I Do It Again?

I have shared my experience with a lot of colleagues who felt the certification was too expensive, to this i always response by saying ignorance comes at a cost too and i am a stickler for knowledge.

Product school has added to my life in terms of knowledge, exposure and being in a community of the people doing the work and walking the talk. I wouldnt change this for the world and would ..definitely..do..it…again

I have plans to attend the leadership product roles and believe that will happen soon

Compared With SAFe PO/PM

Did i tell you that i got a SAFe PO/PM certification too which was a 2day course? That too lifted the darkness on my SAFe knowledge but not sure its comparable to what the good guys at Product School is building. SAFe is a community focussed on Enterprises mostly while product school is for everyone who wants to build a product irrespective of the size. So in order of priorities and value, Product School tops it

An Overload Of Tools

I am still trying to grasp and work with all the tools product school had exposed me to. Some of the ones you will enjoy include

  • Mural
  • Pendo
  • Some analytics tools
  • etc

Final Words

I would recommend product school any time for anyone who can afford it, in my opinion affordability is a relative thing and where there is a will, there is often a way.

If you need any directions, please reach out to me and i am happy to show you whats on offering with product school

content.rendered:
A short story for my former colleagues in the ‘agile framework don’t work” train.

Today I fell off my bike and it was 100% not the fault of my bike.
Same with frameworks. When you fail, check your self and the conditions of your execution. Are your people in the right mindset, the processes alinged with your strategic goals and the people excited, trained and safely prepped to learn, fail and improve?
My trusted bike is like your framework, even if it’s waterfall. It’s totally dependent on you
Today I decided to do a 20miler and got hit with the best London weather – wet conditions
I decided to still ride normally as I would in good conditions (mindset – wrong) expected the same result and failed doing that
Fundamentally, there are conditions required for us humans to set or consider before any framework can optimally deliver value to anyone doing anything.
Are your people prepped for the journey and understand the requirements of the ride?
Are they prepared to fail forward and learn from it – I am definitely not riding fast in wet conditions anymore no matter how tempting the road is
Do you have a RAIDs document to identify these risks and have mitigation plans in place
And do they have fun doing it? Sincerely I was all padded to the teeth today and apart from a small arm sprain I oddly got up from my fall, adjusted the bike and carried on.
Yes, my fall was safe but the truth is that behind every perceived framework fail, people are impacted mentally, physically and often there are loss of jobs

Too often, I have seen organisations put their staff on a bike today and expect them to compete with the Armstrong’s of this world the next day

It doesn’t work that way

My rant is done

excerpt.rendered: Agile Frameworks Don’t work. An experience to shift our mindsets

content.rendered:
As a product management professional in IT, i have worked with many organisations where a roadmap wasn’t well defined or in most cases non existence. Truth is if you are going somewhere and you don’t understand the road or have a map in your hands or your head, chances are high you will fail. Your followers will not know if you are there yet, or what else remains to get to your destination, confusion will blight your delivery and everyone wont be aligned to the cause – getting to a destination predictably. Roadmaps help you reach a destination.

What The Heck Is a Roadmap?

Whether you are embarking on a discovery cause to replicate an Indiana Jones movie, creating products or setting up a business, it is important to be able to predict your journey, understand the trip and be prepared to meet up with potential risks or other issues that will pop up. For example if you were planning to go to the sun, what kind of roadmap would you need? If you were building a house, a digital product or even simply building a website what would be your immediate plan to get these done.

Roadmaps contain two words – a road and a map. A map helps you understand where you are currently and the route to take to reach a destination, and a road usually takes you there.

A roadmap is a written or graphic representation of where a a project or product is currently, outlining where they want the product to go, and the planned initiatives to reach set goals.

Benefits Of A Roadmap

If we know where we are going and understand what we need to do to get there, we are most likely to succeed. A roadmap is central to this, it helps us create a strategy to implement a set of expected actions to achieve a goal. Roadmaps are vital to the success of any project or product delivery. Some of the benefits are listed below

  • It aligns and builds alignment within the team or company
  • It positions everyone in involved for action towards reaching the goal
  • It keeps leadership motivated and in tune with the goals
  • It mentally prepares for the future
  • It helps us identify and plan resources for delivery
  • It helps in communicating the vision
  • It helps us measure success and / or failures

While road-mapping could be a tedious and often demanding procedure – who said planning was easy? – it is vital to every project / product success and should be something every one endeavours to create or participate in. It is the soul of quality delivery, alignment and foundations for valuable conversations even in a product setting

Types Of Roadmaps

While all roadmaps fundamentally create a direction and action for work, there are few different types based on what is to be achieved by a business or how the work is to be done. Mostly a roadmap gets us from point A to point B. FInd below some different types from industires delivering different results

  • An outcome based roadmap is the simplest as it outlines expectations within a period of time – a vision type of roadmap
  • A business roadmap outline the long term strategic plans of any business
  • Timeline roadmaps are usually very popular and serve as delivery plans
  • Agile roadmaps infuses agile development into its iterative work. it is also very flexible and adaptive to changes
  • Tech roadmap is usually geared towards delivering a software

the goals of every roadmap answers three fundamental questions. 1 What are we doing 2. Why are we doing it 3. Who are we doing it for

Last Words

Every expedition has the potential to fail or succeed. Especially if its an unknown territory, the chances of failure are higher. Roadmaps help us visualise behaviours, goals, resources, challenges and other issues that may arise when someone, a business or an organisation decides to build something or achieve something within a defined timeline

Do you have a roadmap in your organisation?

title.rendered: Is having a website in 2021 important?

content.rendered:
We live in a digitally connected world today where websites play an important role. Schools, businesses, individuals and others connect with students buyers, sellers and others through digital media, websites and applications. Today, as consumers, we conduct nearly all our research online. We research in different places, be that search engines, social media, or review sites. And we carry out purchases in lots of different places too. Fundamentally, the internet landscape has changed. But have traditional websites been left behind, or do they still have a place in 2021 and beyond?

As someone who is fascinated by websites and website design, i am of the opinion that having a website is a really valuable investment any blogger, business or organisation should endeavour to take up. A website represents you 24/7/365 when you are offline or closed for other things

Credibility

Undoubtedly, one of the top reasons for having a website is building and retaining credibility. It gives you the ability to promote your products and services in a setting that is of your design, in your brand.

Having a website has additional benefits for credibility too. Including your web address on your social media profiles, business cards, or any other marketing material really goes a long way to prove you’re serious about what you do. It allows people to go check out your credentials and you never know, it could end in a new customer!

Customisation

Free from the rigidity of a social media platform, or a website builder, your website can really look and operate however you want. Of course, you might need some help from a web designer to create a more advanced experience, but the simple ability to control how a page looks and how it reacts helps create a unique and memorable experience.

If you use a popular CMS like WordPress, you can add different features to your website with the click of a button. This could include forms that integrate with your email software, or a chatbot to greet visitors. And if you’re looking to refresh how your website looks, you can roll out a brand new theme with ease.

Expandability

Your website could start small, but the possibilities are endless. As you grow and depending on what you launch with, you could look to add a blog, a portfolio, or maybe even an eCommerce store. You could even launch your own product and have users log in to use it. 

If your website gets popular and you have lots of people arriving and browsing, you can upgrade the technology in the background, such as increasing bandwidth, or even upgrading from shared web hosting to a virtual private server. All of this goes towards creating a smooth, user-friendly experience for your visitors.

It’s never been easier to launch your own website online. With the multitude of tools, free tutorials, and resources available, you can plan out, design and publish a basic website for practically free. Of course, there are costs involved with hosting the website, but it’s incredibly good value for money.

title.rendered: Agile Frameworks Are Like Bikes, Tools For Value Delivery

content.rendered:
I have been in the agile framework environment for a few years and think i can compare my experience with a couple of frameworks in tandem with owning and riding several types of bikes. I am not a professional bike rider but have had my experiences, scars and setbacks with bicycles over time. I have a genuine love for bikes.

A short story

I have owned all a few types of bikes except electric ones. Sincerely I don’t think i will ever own one as i feel much safer in my car than in an electric bike. Now to my short story. A few weeks ago i damaged my precious 6 speed triban500 road bike and had to succumb to riding the alternative or back up unbranded single speed bike.

Career progression takes work, and being part of a herd to let you learn, grow and practice valuable insights is important to helping you succeed in any chosen career. Now to the question – do we need a herd?.

Naturally all humans are part of a herd, whether we are meeting online, in person or a hybrid of both, the herd mindset lives with us. It could be triggered by a common interest, a common goal or even a common problem to solve or try to solve.

What The Heck Do Herds Do?

Fundamentally herds look after each other through empowerment, learning, protection, sharing information and more. I think the biggest and potentially useful herd platform on earth right now is facebook. although on the flip side we are herding with often strangers and allowing these to lead us sometimes in the right direction. find your herd, grow your career

However, in a real valuable herd, identity is key. We know and relate with ourselves on a one to one. We share information and understand the needs of others. We can also upskill and pick up things that can help us for our future

I think herd mentality is a good thing overall. Because if every sheep had to figure out the velocity of the wolf and their personal risk – that would take forever

Neal o barnard

Herds Can Add Value To You

I want to buttress this topic with a true story. We have two kids presently aged 21 and 13. Now both kids have gone through a lot of tough times with us as migrating parents finding our feet in the UK. We have had our share of rough living and sharing apartments with strangers.

However, our second kid has a beautiful heart and is quite excellent at herding and forming friendships. Through this he totally ‘self learned’ how to ride a bike since his herd were bike riders. The amazing thig was that he didnt have a bike at that time as we were struggling as parents to make things wonderful for him.

His big sister on the other hand is less herdy and i could remember teaching her to ride a bike vividly till today

Being part of a herd offers protection for each individual, since one member is often isolated as prey and all the rest take the opportunity to escape. Of course, the entire herd is easily tracked and sighted, which increases the danger, but the risk is much less than for a solitary marriage. There is also greater safety in numbers for animals which have strong defences, such as elephants. Only very strong bull elephants roam alone.

Join A Career Building Herd

Not that your career needs to be able to ride a bike to succeed but if you could both learn to ride one, it would boost your career somewhat.  However, you could boost your career by being part of a herd that is focussed on career growth and improvements.

This could be a platform where you could discuss your goals, problems, be accountable to being more excellent in your chosen career and moving forward with being the best of what you can to make your thrive

I remember way back in Nigeria when we joined a marriage focussed herd called the honourable’s club. We met regularly to discuss everything. It was a platform of laughter, prayer, sharing experiences and setting accountable goals committed to growing our marriage and improving our relationships with one another.

We also had rotational meetings where we met in each others houses, ate, partied, danced and romantically got more attached to our spouses. How i miss that period and still desire such – we might just set one up –

Final Words

To grow your career, you need some directions, help from those who have been in the game before you and also learn the ropes as you go. Be part of a herd today. Find a digital or in person meeting and participate. Commit to growing and it will happen

To your career excellence

title.rendered: The Route To Delivering Great And Functional Products

content.rendered:
The route to delivering great and functional products has evolved over the year. One constant thing to continually consider is the changing customer needs which is evolving at crazy speeds. Often, customers don’t even know what they want. Henry Ford while doing his research and considering ideas to help human transportation asked people what they needed to get them to travel faster ‘A faster horse’ was the response he got, however Henry postulated beyond the limitations of customer experience and built us the first car.

A Product Witch

I remember watching a trailer some time ago where a rich woman came over in a car that ran on some kerosene or some off the shelf fuel. She was branded a ‘witch’ as they had never seen a car before. Luckily she escaped with her life after some mindset coaching to explain a vehicle capable of outrunning a horse and carrying more than one person at a time was already in existence. It took a while but they eventually got used to it.

The world thrives on the ability of ‘product witches’ to be able to bring an idea or opportunity from concept to reality, and often sadly to an end of life. Every product has a life cycle and often evolves into something else to extend its existence.

The world is experiencing hybrid cars, electric cars, Tesla, and the rest of them are thriving on the fact that an idea that made no sense to the common man is making life convenient in the form of a car that does not use oil or diesel. At the moment, hydro fuelled cars are being researched and being created and should hit the markets soon.

Product management rules the world. Products come in different forms, shapes and deliver different values to the end user

The Product Journey

Here’s an overview video of the product development life cycle. We’ll cover topics mentioned here in-depth in the rest of the course.  

As you watch the following video, look out for the answers to these questions:

  1. Where do I start from?
  2. When should you think of ideas vs. opportunities?
  3. When do we start building?
  4. What comes after all that?
  5. How do we evolve further?

Where Do We Start From

Every product has an end user goal, it is not usually about creating a new feature driven at changing ways of doing things or some other valuable goal. A product seeks to deliver value in the simplest possible way. A Porsche and a VW both carry people from A to B but we know both are cars but cost differently. A VW is most likely driven by people who earn less that those who drive a Porsche. In every product, the end user needs, wants, lifestyle, income and other defining attributes come to play. Without this we might build a product nobody wants, can afford or is suitable for their lifestyle or needs

An Idea Or An Opportunity

Products evolve from ideas and /or opportunities or gaps identified in the market or within customers. Presently I work as a volunteer for Grant A Smile as a webmaster and here is the story.

A teacher notices a child who is in a really dirty state, unkempt and is being bullied by her classmates. This goes on for a while and nothing seems to change. She investigates and finds out that the child is a ‘carer to a parent suffering from terminal disease and live in a really depressing environment – house full of clutter – and minimum care from the parent. She tries to notify social care but gets no response for a while.

She identifies a gap and an opportunity to set up ‘Grant A Smile’ an award winning UK charity set up to grant holiday wishes and more to young people living with disease and terminal illness, they also provide decluttering services and shopping to families impacted.

Over three years later – Grant A Smile is thriving and getting so much visibility and support from all over UK and they plan to make this a National Service across the UK and beyond. Today they have become self subsistent by offering office cleaning services to generate revenue and provide services to more families across the Greater London axes. Read the story here.

A product can come from an idea or an opportunity.

When To Start Building

Setting up a team to build a product isn’t usually a walk in the park, it takes understanding, tradeoffs, setting priorities and really agreeing on what to start off with. In Product management, the term MVP is used to align teams to look forward to what to release in the market. Also, a methodology called agile helps the team deliver in testable increments which can be adapted to changing customer needs as it is needed. Teams work in an incremental way to deliver value and come up with a product that meets the Minimum Viable Goal.

What Comes After That?

A product can go through several releases until it meets the end goal set forth by the product manager or the business. There is usually a vision for the product which is decomposed into daily or regular activities to collectively meet this identified and socialised vision. A product has so many sides and different aligned teams work on these to provide value and create a single product that delivers all the identified persona requirements.

Product team members can include – product management, marketing, User experience, User Interactions/Interface, Design etc All these work together to bring the product to life in terms of value

Once a product is done – it is launched and pushed to end users through identified strategies – some include freemium, 30day trials, free to use etc

Evolving The Product

Every product follows the below life cycle

  • Introduction of the product
  • Growth (or decline) of the product
  • Maturity of the product
  • Decline of the product

Where a product does not evolve, it would die. Think Nokia, Blackberry, Netscape etc.

Final Words About Product Delivery

In conclusion, product management has its good and bad sides and is usually a function of the culture of the organisation delivering the product. Two main takeaways for your thinking as shown below

  • Remember, the solution does not matter. The process to get to the solution matters.
  • You cannot win by yourself. You have to take all of the stakeholders together to win.

title.rendered: Some Responsibilities of a Business Analyst

content.rendered:
The definitions of the role of a business analyst have evolved over the years. Considering the shift from waterfall methodologies to more recent agile ways of working, this has impacted the demands on the capabilities of the role. Business Analysis is a worthy designation in the field of business and innovation. A business analyst has multiple responsibilities and roles to play. This particular designation has a huge demand in the field of technology and business. The changing domain knowledge of the business world also has an impact on the business analyst field. Examples include cloud-enhanced technologies like CRM, AI, Machine Learning, and more. Others include Robotics Process Automation, Software Development, Mobile Applications, Learning Management Systems, and more.

To succeed as a business analyst requires some technical and/or business background. Nowadays, you also require some domain knowledge to help add value to your business or employer

Find listed below some of the key responsibilities of a business analyst.

Roles Of A Business Analyst-

Let us talk about the role of a business analyst. A business analyst would be able to fit into the role of an intermediator, connecter and it proceeds to several other roles as well. However, the predominant role consists of assembling new ideas, resources and implementing them into the system. This means the role of a business analyst is to make sure that everything is functioning in a proper way. Nowadays, business analysts evolve to become product owners, delivery managers, scrum masters, and more

Business analysis is considered to be the core procedure of most businesses and their evolution. The analyst needs to interact with the various departments such as marketing head, salesforce, production, accounting, human resource, and so on. As a business analyst, you need to keep track of the latest trends and techniques in order to survive in this changing business horizon.

  • Analyzing and evaluating the current business processes a company has and identifying areas of improvement
  • Researching and reviewing up-to-date business processes and new IT advancements to make systems more modern
  • Presenting ideas and findings
  • Training and coaching staff members
  • Creating Design initiatives depending on the business’s requirements and needs
  • Collaborating with users and stakeholders
  • Domain knowledge
  • Understanding the various requirements
  • Working on the details
  • Functional and Non Functional Requirements
  • User/Business Acceptance Testing

Top 5 responsibilities of a business analyst-

  1. Understanding various requirements-

Talking about the responsibilities of a business analyst, this one comes at first. The primary responsibility of a business analyst is to interact with the stakeholders in order to have a better understanding of their requirements and then discuss it with the project developers. As a business analyst, you need to amass all the requirements of your project from the business stakeholders and work as a mediator between the stakeholders and the developers. Your job will include attending several meetings with the stakeholders for this purpose.

  1. Presenting Ideas And Findings

For each and every business, business analysts are expected to be highly efficient in public speaking and presentation skills. As an analyst, your responsibility is to deliver and present presentations on the scenario of the business, designs, and as well as future prospects of the business. An impressive presentation by the analyst can be effective enough on the growth of the particular business. As a business analyst, your job is to impress your client and stakeholders with impressive presentations. If you think your speaking skills need to be improved, you can sign up for online coaching for public speaking.

  1. Working on the details-

Here comes the most important responsibility of a business analyst. A business analyst should have intricate details about the requirements of the project. As a Business Analyst, you should examine the requirements of the project and make sure that the other teams have the whole details. Here, the business analysts need to spend a lot of time in meeting with the stakeholders and the customers. The Business analysts are known to assemble the requirements and functional specifications which are accepted by the company and the developers for the implementation purpose.

  1. Functional and non-functional requirements-

Requirements are the main working documents of any project. This helps to define the scope of the work and manage the overall expectations of everyone involved in the project. This is a major responsibility of the business analyst and is a product of an accurate discovery and collaboration with business representatives and end-users. A business analyst should be able to works on classifying and evaluate the functional as well as non-functional needs.  He should have a clear idea of what the project would offer (functional) and how would the project work(non-functional).

  1. User/Business Acceptance testing-

The business analysts make sure that the product delivered by the company, fulfills the requirements of the user and is functioning well. So, business and/or user acceptance testing is one of the vital responsibilities of a business analyst. The business analyst prepares the test plans and guides the business to execute these.

6. Training and coaching staff members

The business Analyst is responsible for engaging the business and ensuring users have an understanding of new platforms, software and more. He /she helps with training documentation and coaching of end-users who could be staff members, customers, end-users, and more.

7. Creating Design initiatives depending on the business’s requirements and needs

The Business Analyst is also responsible as part of the design team for designing solutions to meet business requirements and needs. This could be a collection of interviews, workshops, and even persona definition sessions to fine-tune solutions and designs that could benefit the business and end-users.

8.Collaborating with users and stakeholders

One of the core responsibilities of the analyst is a constant collaboration with all players in a business or project setup. While the analyst is product and value-driven, unlike the project manager who manages scope, budgets and timelines.

9. Domain Knowledge

With the evolving business landscapes with changing solutions, business solutions, with examples including Agile, Waterfall methodologies, Content Management Systems, Cloud Technologies, Cybersecurity advancements, Robotics Process Automation, Machine Learning, and more. Being abreast with these solutions and ways of working will stand you apart and make your skills attractive to potential hiring managers

title.rendered: Essential Skills for A Successful Business Analyst Career

content.rendered:
Some Essential Business Analyst Skills and Abilities –

Business analysts provide an essential service to businesses everywhere. We save time, money and ensure expected quality levels are met by our potentials. Whatever it is anyone is delivering, customising or developing, the Business Analayst is the one stop shop provider from discovery to delivery and business as usual. Below, we will find out basic skills needed by a business analyst to win in the game

  • Communication Skills
  • Technical Skills
  • Analytical Skills
  • Documentation Skills
  • Problem Solving Skills
  • Decision-Making Skills
  • Managerial Skills
  • Negotiation and Persuasion Skills
  • Communication Skills

  • By nature of the job, Business Analysts spend a great deal of time interacting with users, clients, vendors, management and development teams. A project’s success may depend upon our clear communicating details like project requirements, requested changes and testing results. Fluent language skills and written communication abilities are necessary to thrive in our career as a Business Analyst.
  • Technical Skills
    In order to identify business solutions, we should know what information technology applications are being utilized, what new possible outcomes can be achieved through current platforms and what the latest technology offers.
    Testing software and designing business systems are also important technical business analyst skills. Gaining respect and creating a sense of confidence among IT and business end-users requires us to speak with confidence about business and technology, and to demonstrate a strong technical aptitude.
  • Analytical Skills
    A BA skill set should include outstanding analytical skills so that a customer’s business needs are properly interpreted and translated into application and operational requirements. One aspect of our role is analyzing data, documents, user input surveys and workflow to determine which course of action will correct the business problem. Strong analytical skills are beneficial in performing our job successfully.
  • Documentation Skills
    The ability to produce high-quality documents, written for their intended audience, is a must-have skill for any and all Business Analysts. Either in Microsoft Word, Google Docs or Apple Pages, we need to gather templates and keep them in our arsenal. The ability to create a well thought out cover page, clickable index, high-level overview and the ability to embed spreadsheets, process flows diagrams, presentation slides and then end with strong, well though out and researched recommendation, will offer senior stakeholders the ability to make major decisions from our documents.
  • Problem Solving Skills
    While the ability to create workable solutions to business problems is not unique to business analysts, it is a necessary skill for performing our job successfully. As with most IT roles, the business analyst’s career may be spent dealing with frequent and random changes. When we are working to develop custom business solutions, nothing is 100% predictable – so finding ways to quickly resolve problems and move toward a project’s successful completion is important in our role.
  • Decision-Making Skills
    Another important Business Analyst skill is the ability to make decisions. As a consultant to management and advisor to developers, we are called upon for sound judgment in a wide variety of business matters, any number of which could determine the viability of the business. Professionals who wish to pursue a Business Analyst career should be able to assess a situation, receive input from stakeholders, and select a course of action.
  • Managerial Skills
    Another skill we should possess is the ability to manage projects. Planning the project scope, directing staff members, handling change requests, forecasting budgets and keeping everyone on the project within allotted time constraints are just some of the management skills we should possess. Supervising projects of all sizes, from inception to implementation (and usually concurrently) can take a high degree of managerial skill.
  • Negotiation and Persuasion Skills
    We as a Business Analyst serve as a liaison between developers and users, clients and companies, and management and IT. Finding the balance between individual wants and business needs, and then interacting with a variety of personality types toward a solution that works for the business, takes professional persuasion skills. When competing for client projects, our negotiation skills come into frequent use, with the goal of achieving a profitable outcome for the company and a working solution for the client. Maintaining relationships within an organization and with external partners is an important function of a Business Analyst that require strong negotiation and persuasion skills.

title.rendered: Benefits Of Writing Blog Articles For Your Business

content.rendered:
We live in an age where content is king and being able to create content is a helpful skill. Doing this connects us through the printed page either digitally or through physical media such as a book or otherwise. As a mentor and analyst, being able to express my opinion, thoughts and experience in a blog is empowering, releiveing and an awesome feeling

What Is A Blog

Blogs have been around for a while and have provided platforms for learning, information dissemination, and empowerment. It can be defined in simple words as a regularly updated website or web page, typically one run by anyone, that is written in an informal or conversational style. It is designed to engage, build or express a line of thought and create opportunities for engagement. Using wordpress as a reference, a blog is an online journal or informational website, with the most recent posts appearing at the top of the page. Blogs are often run by people who want to share their views and opinions on particular subjects or topics. Fashion, food, and travel blogs are among the most popular. Blogs can contain photos and videos, surveys, forms, as well as text.

Your blog must offer some value to the potential reader

Marketers often use blogs, in addition to social platforms like Twitter, to communicate with their market and build rapport.

Businesses often incorporate blogs into their main corporate websites and use them to provide information to customers and prospective customers, keep them informed of upcoming events and update them on the latest happenings. Blogs help stay afloat and afresh.

Why blog?

A blog is fundamentally a tool to share information. While it should provide some value to the reader, its often used to motivate the user to perform an action such as buy a product, subscribe to a service or something else. Blogs should help with a question, provide option, help a line of thought or just make someone laugh. A blog can contain poetry, reviews, teachings, reports, experience, news information and more. A blog post helps your website stay fresh on the world wide web and allows google bots and the like scan and be attracted to your website and content.

  • Attract potential customers through content
  • Establish some authority
  • Build some relationship with customers by providing help
  • Build awareness of a brand, product, or service
  • Drive traffic to their main website or online store
  • Help answer a question or concern

Thinking of Starting a blog?

Writing and managing a blog could be a worthwhile action if well managed and faithfully done. It is time-consuming and involves a lot of time and effort to build. Successful blogs take time, resources, and the commitment to make it happen. Also, there is the potential for your blog to be monetized through ads and other opportunities that abound out there. Google Adsense, Ezoic, and a few others provide opportunities for monetization of your blog. A successful blog is not promised but will be a result of some of the actions listed below.

 Blogging is still an extremely viable and effective medium for creating content and building an online business, even today

  • Researching topics, structuring your content, and editing your blog
  • Sourcing images and videos – Unsplash and Pixabay offer free images to get you started
  • Posting on a regular basis – at least a blog a day
  • Responding to readers questions where you allow commenting in your blog
  • Monetizing your blog when your readership has grown
  • Hiring content writers as your blog grows in size
  • Deciding on a niche for your blog

Blogging platforms are a type of web CMS designed to simplify the creation and maintenance of blogs. Blogs are text and image-heavy websites that get updated over time with new content; updates are called blog posts.

Starting a blog isn’t a walk in the park. It takes commitment, the will to succeed, and endurance. It’s usually worth the time when the results come to light.

The Process of Blogging

Get started with your blog by following these steps:

  • Choose the niche you’d like to focus on. Decide on your passion here. Streamline your options to what works for you. FOcussing on a niche creates the ability for you to follow your passion and become a potential authority on that topic and be more effective in helping those who visit your blog. On the other side, if you run out of ideas, you can widen your reach by diversifying your content.
  • Choosing a domain name. A domain name is the first doorway to your website/blog. It is the first implication or direction A domain name should show the user what your blog is potentially about as it is the title for your blog. Is should be easy to remember and simple enough to stay in memory It should be descriptive of your blog and may include a keyword. Domain names are increasingly popular and quite affordable to buy from popular resellers and other services.
  • Choose a blogging platform. There are varieties of blogging platforms you can use to create your blog, most of which provide free versions for users to get started with. WordPress, is a popular platform and website for beginners and professionals are a great choice for beginners. On a free platform, ads will be run on your site and you may never actually have full ownership of it. . For a business endeavor, choosing a paid platform in which you host your own blog is highly recommended: Popular Blogging Platforms are listed below
  1. WordPress – Most popular blogging platform
  2. Tumblr – Best blogging platform for microblogging
  3. Squarespace
  4. Blogger – Best free blogging platform
  5. Wix 
  6. Medium

Furthermore in considering the platform to use, you want to consider the following features and capabilities for your blog

  • Theme Repository
  • Commenting System
  • WYSIWYG Editor
  • Publishing Tools for Managing Content
  • Sharing and Distribution Capabilities
  • Media Management (Videos and Images)
  • Performance Tracking
  • Administration and User Management
  • Custom Content Types
  • Decide on your host and theme. A blog host is a company that provides space on its servers, for a fee, to store your blog. There are many to choose from. When choosing a host, as well as considering cost, consider whether it offers a reliable service and enough server space. When you have chosen a host, you can put your blog up online and install a theme. A theme is a template that can enhance the look and feel of your blog. You can access a free theme or purchase one. You can also install plugins to improve functionality.

Step 5: Create your content. The final step is to create your content. Remember, the more you blog, the better you will get at it. So now it’s time to start writing.

Expected Frequency Of blogging

It is expected that if you want your blog to add some value or make and impact, it should be a daily activity. Quality blogging will take time, dedication, research and the will to succeed.

It is expected from research and experience that an effective blog should answer a question, provide a direction, opinion, or basically help out with a problem. It should be about 1,500 words and provide a subject. Aim to cover topics in as much depth as you can, so the blog really offers value to potential readers and visitors to your website.

Your blog must provide quality. answer a question and generally be the go-to for an answer, help, or list of todos to guide productivity. The better your blog provides some kind of value to your readers, the more they will come back for more and even share your blog and content with friends and associates. In blogging, quality trumps quantity.

Choosing a Niche/Topic?

When it comes to topics to blog about, the list is endless. When choosing a topic, try to think of one that:

  • Provides relevant information
  • Demonstrates a unique solution
  • Shows you offer some help to your readers
  • Provides some value to your readers
  • Shares detailed and helpful information

Good topics for a blog can include some of the below listed:

  • An experience you would like to share with the world eg lockdown during Covid19
  • Explaining how someone used your product or service in a humorous way
  • showcasing a great product you have used yourself
  • An interview with an influencer, musician or uprising star

Promoting my blog to the world?

At the end of the day, you want your blog to be read by as many people as possible. The best way of achieving this is to create high quality, original content on a consistent basis that readers look forward to reading, find extremely useful – and are keen to share.

To ensure your blog reaches the widest possible audience:

  • Promote your blog on your social media platforms
  • Include your blog link in your social media profiles
  • Share your blog posts as soon as you publish them
  • Share your posts on networks that you know your audience uses
  • Share new blog posts more than once
  • Review your older posts, update them if necessary, and share the best ones again
  • Include links to your blog in your email signature
  • Apply to have your blog content present on social bookmarking sites
  • Invite other bloggers to guest post on your site, and vice versa

Promoting your blog should never be an after-thought. After all, it’s important that you get the best return from all the time you spend creating your content. So promote it far and wide – and on a continuous basis. That way, you’ve got the best chance of reaching the widest possible audience, increasing traffic to your site, and attracting potential new customers.

Now you’ve got all the basic tips and tricks you need to start blogging. So why wait until tomorrow? Get off the sideline, jump right in, and give blogging a try today!

Where do i come in to help in all of these?

With experience in content design and a student of project24 at income school, I can help with your blogging strategy and other things that need to be added to get the maximum of the effort.

Over the years I have been engaged in enterprise transformation projects usually with multiple workstreams, (robotic) process automation to improve customer engagement, enabling teams via agile delivery strategies (product ownership and scrum master roles). I have helped and enabled delivery teams to understand the need for a product vision and understanding of the release plan to enable incremental value added to the customer journey and service design across financial services, private business, and the public sector. Agility is the ability to deliver customer-centered changes, products or increment of work as quickly as possible. It is responding to change and bringing customer centered creativity to the market. It is meeting a need, a culture, mindset and a way of working

Organizational agility simply refers to the adoption of customer-centered delivery techniques from ‘top-down’. Agility is a mindset, a way of working, a different paradigm that is achievable through practice, doing and continuously doing.

The pillars of agile should drive any initiation of agile practices in any organisation. These are Transparency, Adaption and Inspection

Company Vision and strategy

In understanding your organisational vision and strategy, the following questions have to be answered. A discovery of your culture, behaviours and respond to change needs to be assessed, documented and discussed

  • What to this company is the goal of improving agility? Why an agile route?
  • What are your organizational goals and how does the role you’re trying to fill expected to help to achieve those goals?
  • What key results would you expect to happen?
  • Who is currently involved with this effort?
  • Does management fully support these efforts?
  • Who determines your product strategy?
  • What are the product and company goals for this year, how do they connect?
  • Are company goals being met or on track?
  • Is the present culture enabling agility.
  • What strategies do you have in place to manage change and resistance to the same.

Customer collaboration

Customers are key to your profit and growth. Developing a continuous relationship with your customers will move you forward as a business

  • How involved are the business and stakeholders/customers in product development?
  • How are end-users being involved in UAT and others?
  • Do you have a fully detailed knowledge of your end-users

Measurements

  • Are you measuring impact/value? If yes, how? If no, what are you measuring?
  • Do you ever go back to existing features? to see how they perform?
  • Do you measure team performance? How?
  • What do you expect of me? What is the measurement of my success?

Your Teams

  • Are teams trusted to manage their own work/sprint?
  • Is there a general trust in people and teams?
  • Can teams change the way they work? What would be the limit?
  • Do teams have clear goals?
  • Are team goals generally being met?
  • How are teams created?
  • Can each team fully independently get work from todo to done?
  • Who decides when something is done?
  • How often does extra stress/panic/disruption of work occur?

Technological Solutions

  • Do you employ continuous integration or comparable techniques?
  • What automated tests do you use?
  • What other tests do you use?
  • How hard is it to release a change?
  • Do developers enjoy the current tech stack?

Agile approaches

  • Are you using any frameworks or methodology? Fully? Hybrid? Why?
  • How do you determine the right framework or methodology?

Community input

– How do they make decisions? E.g. Is it the highest person in hierarchy vs the expert vs the engagement of impacted
– What is the change model in their heads? E.g. is it A –> B defined process with metrics, sticks, and carrots OR a journey without defined end, but checks for direction and correction course (metrics, carrots, and sticks still) OR is it a model which recognizes personal perspectives and stages of change.
– What they think is a role of management? E.g. managing people, assigning work and controlling work (Tailorism) vs Developing people, servant leadership, changing organisation (e.g. through system thinking, theory of constraints).

“Why do want to implement the Agile way of working and change the organisation to the Agile mindset”

“How will the top of the organisation support/propagate this change?”

“Are they willing to be coached too?”

“How many mandates do I get?”

“Are people going to be or are they Agile trained?”

Can you give an example of non-agile patterns or behaviors in your organization that you want to change, reduce or eliminate?

What is your definition of an Agile Mindset?

Why do you love working here?

Can you talk me through how a piece of code goes through from development to production?

Do devs work directly with customers or do all customer interactions go through the PO?
